message.content:
Build the UI for a native webmail client at `/dashboard/mail` in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 + Tailwind, dark-navy + violet Nxeon theme). Match this target design (a modern email client, on-brand): a left **folder rail** (Compose button, Inbox/Starred/Snoozed/Sent/Drafts/Spam/Trash/Archive with unread counts, custom Folders section, a Tools section, and a **storage bar** at the bottom "X GB / Y GB used"), a **message list** column (folder title + unread count, Primary/Promotions/Social-style filter tabs, rows with avatar-initials, sender, subject, snippet, time, star, unread dot, pagination), a **reading pane** (subject, from/to, date, action toolbar: Archive/Delete/Snooze/Move/Reply/Reply-all/Forward, the message body, and a **Quick Reply** box), and a right **contact/detail panel** (sender contact info, tags). Study `app/(marketing)/vibe-coding/page.tsx` and `components/portal/*` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` first to match the exact design language (fonts, cards, colors, the NXEON look). Make it genuinely beautiful and consistent with the rest of the portal — this replaces the dated SOGo webmail.

The BACKEND is built by another agent. Call these server actions (import from `@/lib/actions-mail`) and use the types from `@/lib/mail/types` (READ that file — do not change it): `getMailboxes()`, `listFolders()`, `listMessages(folder, page, search?)`, `getMessage(folder, uid)`, `sendMessage(payload)`, `setFlag(folder, uid, flag, value)`, `moveMessage(folder, uid, toFolder)`, `deleteMessage(folder, uid)`. Attachments download from `/api/mail/attachment?folder=&uid=&part=`.

Only create/edit under: `app/dashboard/mail/` (a `page.tsx` server component that does the initial `requireUser` + first `listFolders`/`listMessages` and renders the client), and `components/customer/mail/*` (e.g. `MailClient.tsx` the client shell, `FolderRail.tsx`, `MessageList.tsx`, `ReadingPane.tsx`, `Composer.tsx`, `ContactPanel.tsx`). Do NOT touch lib/, app/api, the admin/marketing trees, or the app/dashboard/layout nav (I'll wire the sidebar link separately). 

Key requirements:
- Client-side state for selected folder / selected message / compose-open; fetch via the server actions (wrap in `useTransition`, show loading skeletons, handle empty states like "No messages" cleanly).
- **Render the email HTML body inside a sandboxed `<iframe sandbox="" srcDoc={html}>`** (no allow-scripts, no allow-same-origin) so hostile email HTML can't run — this is required for security. Show plaintext fallback when no html.
- Compose/Reply modal: to/cc/subject/body, calls `sendMessage`; Reply prefills to + subject "Re:" + quoted body + `inReplyToUid`.
- Star toggles `setFlag(...,"flagged")`; opening a message clears unread; Archive/Delete call move/delete and update the list optimistically.
- Responsive: on mobile it collapses to list → reading pane. Respect the mockup's polish (avatars as colored initials, unread dots, tag chips, the storage bar).

CRITICAL: Do NOT run `npm run build`/`next build` (it races with the backend agent). Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files — some action imports may not exist until the backend agent finishes; if tsc complains only about missing `@/lib/actions-mail` exports, note it and continue, the parent integrates). Do NOT run git. Report the components built and how you matched the target design.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

The container's max-width of 1280px is actually sufficient for a 4-column email layout, so I can design a responsive multi-column mail client that fits within those constraints while using the full available height as a tall card-based interface. I'll hide the contact panel below xl since max-w-7xl constrains the layout anyway, giving the reading pane enough breathing room at wider breakpoints. Now I'm planning the component structure: a server component for the mail page, a client wrapper, and separate components for the folder rail, message list, reading pane, composer, and contact panel. I need to define the server action signatures I'll be calling, starting with `getMailboxes()` to fetch the available mailboxes. I'll write a helper function that can handle both cases—whether `getMailboxes()` returns a single `MailboxInfo` object or an array of them—so I can safely extract the mailbox data regardless of the actual signature. I'll use Array.isArray to safely handle both cases — if getMailboxes returns a single MailboxInfo or an array, the check narrows the type correctly and TypeScript accepts it either way without errors.

Better approach: have the server component call getMailboxes, normalize the result, and pass the resolved MailboxInfo as a prop to the client component. Then I need to define the API methods — listFolders, listMessages, getMessage, sendMessage, setFlag, moveMessage, and deleteMessage — each with their expected signatures and return types. For sendMessage I'll just await it without depending on a specific return shape.

Now for the folder sidebar: the design wants Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Sent, Drafts, Spam, Trash, and Archive, but the backend's listFolders returns roles like inbox, sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive, and custom — there's no starred or snoozed role since those are virtual. I'll treat Starred and Snoozed as UI-only items that don't map directly to backend folders.

For Starred, I can implement it as a virtual filter that loads the inbox and shows only flagged messages client-side. It's not a true folder, but it'll work functionally without needing pagination complexity.

Snoozed has no backend support, so I'll add it as a virtual folder with an empty state message. The sidebar layout will follow a clear structure: the main folders (Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Sent, Drafts, Spam, Trash, Archive), then a Folders section for custom ones, and a Tools section with simple action buttons like Refresh and Settings, plus the storage bar at the bottom.

For the Tools section, I'll keep it minimal and honest—Refresh will actually reload the folders and message list, and Settings will link to the email dashboard. The filter tabs (Primary, Promotions, Social) don't have backend category support, so I'll implement them as client-side heuristic filters that categorize messages based on keywords and sender domains.

For counts, I'll show unread numbers from MailFolder where available, and compute starred counts from the loaded messages themselves—omitting counts for virtual folders where the data isn't reliable. Now I'm moving on to the reading pane toolbar, where I need to wire up Archive (moving to the archive folder), Delete (moving to trash), and Move (with a folder dropdown), while keeping Snooze as a disabled coming-soon feature.

Quick replies will send through the message API with the inReplyToUid reference, and I'll apply optimistic updates to remove messages from the list immediately on archive or delete. Star toggling will call setFlag with "seen" as the flag parameter, updating the list optimistically as well.

For avatars, I'm generating colored initials from the sender's name or email address, using a hash function to map to a consistent hue. I'll keep the helper utilities within the components for now rather than extracting to a shared file.

I'm organizing the mail component structure with a utils file for avatar colors, initials, date formatting, and icons, then building out MailClient as the orchestration hub with FolderRail, MessageList, ReadingPane, ContactPanel, and Composer as child components. I'll define the virtual folder concept within MailClient to manage the folder state.

For virtual folders like Starred and Snoozed, I'm using special sentinels like `__starred__` and `__snoozed__` to distinguish them from actual IMAP paths. When a virtual folder is selected, I'll load messages from the inbox and filter by flags for Starred, while Snoozed will remain empty for now. The pagination won't be perfectly accurate for virtual folders, but that's acceptable as a tradeoff for simplicity.

I'm going to build the folder rail data by combining real folders with virtual items in the MailClient, then start implementing the utilities. For the message list, I'll show the time if the message is from today, otherwise just the short date. Let me write the util file now.

## Summary

Built a complete native webmail client at `/dashboard/mail`, matching the target design and the NXEON dark-navy/violet design language (studied `vibe-coding/page.tsx`, `components/portal/Shell.tsx`, `primitives.tsx`, and `globals.css` to reuse `card`, `glass`, `btn-primary`, `nav-item-active`, `section-label`, `input`, `skeleton`, brand colors, and the `animate-fade-up` motion).

### Files created (all under the allowed paths)
- `app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx` — server component: `requireUser()`, initial `listFolders()` + `getMailboxes()` + `listMessages(inbox,1)`, renders the client. Falls back to a branded `EmptyState` ("No mailbox connected" → link to `/dashboard/email`) if mail isn't provisioned.
- `components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx` — client shell holding all state (selected folder / message / compose), `useTransition` for list loads, optimistic mutations, debounced search, toasts, and the responsive 4-column grid.
